A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we study the tradeoff between sparsity and volatility in the design of mean-reverting portfolios, which is an important issue in the design of profitable trading strategies.
, when trading mean-reverting portfolios, one needs to consider carefully tradeoffs between portfolio size and volatility.
the problem of finding the best mean-reverting portfolio can be cast as an integer programming problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of finding a maximally mean-reverting portfolio that is both sparse and volatile is an interesting and challenging problem.
the search for sparse mean-reverting portfolios is a hard problem, whose difficulty increases with the number of assets considered.
, in order to be profitable, a mean-reverting portfolio must be sparse, volatile and mean-reverting at the same time.
